legend: Exons and intronic breakpoints of the ABL1 and BCR genes (blue horizontal arrows) and the corresponding fusion proteins. In the BCR gene, the most frequently observed major breakpoint cluster region (M-bcr), the less frequently observed minor breakpoint cluster region (m-bcr), and the rarely observed micro breakpoint cluster region (µ-bcr) can produce eight mRNA fusion transcripts and translated proteins due to alternate splicing of exon 2 of the ABL1 gene and due to two internal breakpoints in introns 13 and 14 of the BCR gene (note: length of exons and introns not to scale). In addition, three variant breakpoint cluster regions (v-bcr; blue vertical arrows) have been described rarely or only once. ABL1b is a pseudogene and is spliced out frequently.

diagnosis: Chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) in the chronic phase at diagnosis
legend: Smear from bone marrow aspirate. A non-lobulated micromegakaryocyte with cytoplasm showing mature staining properties and a granular structure. The average cell diameter is < 25 μm. Dysplastic megakaryocytic features (namely hypolobation) and micromegakaryocytes are consistently seen in all paediatric patients with CML.
source: Photograph by courtesy of Dr. Sabrina Bouyer, Laboratoire d’hématologie, Centre Hospitalier Universitaire, Poitiers, France.

diagnosis: Chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) in the chronic phase at diagnosis
legend: An increased number of eosinophils (arrows) can be found at all stages of maturation in most paediatric patients with CML. The number of basophils (arrowheads) in chronic-phase CML is usually slightly increased, but in advanced CML, marked and sometimes even excessive basophilia is a key laboratory finding.

diagnosis: Chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML) in the chronic phase at diagnosis
legend: Smear from bone marrow aspirate. Hypersegmented neutrophils (arrow: a nucleus with > 4 segments) can be detected frequently in chronic-phase CML because of the prolonged lifetime of the mature granulocytes. Immature and mature eosinophils (arrowheads) may also show basophilic granules and are termed “harlequin cells” by some authors.

CML in the chronic phase at diagnosis (bone marrow trephine biopsy). Histology demonstrates increased and left-shifted granulopoiesis. In such cases, there is an accompanying proliferation of eosinophils and eosinophilic precursors, a reduction of erythropoiesis, and an accumulation of small, non-lobulated megakaryocytes.

tablehtml:
Chronic phase

Presence of all of the following criteria:

< 10% blasts in the peripheral blood and/or bone marrow

 

Does not meet any criteria for accelerated phase or blast phase

 

Accelerated phase

Presence of any of the following criteria:

Peripheral blood and/or bone marrow blasts 10–19%

 

Persistently high or increasing white blood cell count unresponsive to therapy

 

Persistent thrombocytosis > 1000 × 109/L uncontrolled by therapy, or persistent thrombocytopenia < 100 × 109/L unrelated to therapy

 

Peripheral blood basophils ≥ 20%

 

Persistent or increasing splenomegaly

 

Any new clonal abnormality or additional clonal abnormalities in Philadelphia (Ph) chromosome–positive cells at diagnosis (second Ph chromosome clone, trisomy 8 or 19, isochromosome 17q), abnormalities of 3q26.2, or complex karyotype

 

Provisional criteria:

Poor therapy response (lack of haematological response to first tyrosine kinase inhibitor or molecular indication of resistance to two sequential tyrosine kinase inhibitors) or

 

Occurrence of mutations in BCR::ABL1 during tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy

 

Blast phase

Presence of all of the following criteria:

Peripheral blood and/or bone marrow blasts constituting ≥ 20% of the peripheral blood white blood cell count or nucleated bone marrow cells

 

Persistently high or increasing white blood cell count unresponsive to therapy

 

Extramedullary blast proliferation

 

Bona fide lymphoblasts in the blood or bone marrow, even if < 10% (may indicate imminent lymphoblastic transformation); in such cases, further clinical and genetic investigations are suggested
